candidates.license: Apache-2.0; README and deployment POM, not MIT
candidates.dependencies: Java 11 source/target; generated ANTLR parser and antlr4-runtime [4.7,); optional Stanford CoreNLP [1.2.0,)
candidates.contract: Caller supplies tokens with nullable String-valued attributes. Sequence operators, ordered search/backtracking, alternative and same-span conjunction, greedy/reluctant repetition and captures. Attribute regex calls java.util.regex.Pattern on one attribute. Does not lex source text.
candidates.complexity: Backtracking endpoint iterators and branch state stack; no demonstrated linear worst-case bound or measured Java 21 throughput. Caller token attribute access can occur repeatedly.
candidates.java21_fit: No full donor build run. Uses reflection for Pattern.namedGroups; this is public in target Java 21, so do not assert module-access failure. Unbounded ANTLR dependency needs qualification before any convergence build.
candidates.decision: REFERENCE_ONLY_FOR_GPL_RECEIVER; full grammar is not supplied by existing Synexia glob; choose target-owned Pattern.Node/Matcher for bounded typed token builders, no Apache expression pasted into GPL owner

candidates.contract: Concatenates angle-bracket token markers without escaping token payload; rewrites token expression then splits reported marker spans. Current pinned source uses redos/third-party regex with compile guards and a timeout, rather than older rendered documentation bare re.findall.

counterexample.implication: Encoding cannot distinguish one token from two and cannot guarantee arbitrary token boundaries.

candidates.complexity: Includes serialization allocation plus regex engine work; source timeout is not a proof of a linear bound. No runtime benchmark performed.
candidates.java21_fit: Python implementation, not a Java or JNI donor

candidates.license: Proprietary SDK EULA with conditional community/commercial eligibility and restrictions on redistribution and competing standalone interfaces; not an open-source code donor
candidates.contract: Token definitions precede pattern matching and can classify words, numbers, string literals and brackets. Lexical state supplies structural awareness; named captures alone do not.

Literal resolver tokens, question mark for exactly one token, star for any token sequence and escaping. Boolean matches/lookingAt/find, resolver identity admission. No capture groups, match spans, arbitrary attribute grammar or Java lexical safety.
candidates.complexity: Long frontier up to 63 atoms; BitSet correctness path beyond, per-token state iteration. Required token signal can reject candidates; no measured receiver threshold.
candidates.java21_fit: Existing convergence owner depends on resolver, tokenizer and progress monitor; not a public JDK owner

candidates.license: SPDX Apache-2.0 AND MIT; source credits William Fiset KMP recurrence and references retained donor/license documents
candidates.contract: Exact long-token matching, compact alphabet/KMP failure/DFA, limits on dense transition table and work, composable summaries and repeated composition. Does not parse regex, normalize text or capture arbitrary regex groups.
candidates.complexity: Dense state-by-alphabet memory with explicit admission limits; exact-token scans and logarithmic repeated summary composition. No new receiver benchmark here.

candidates.license: Existing target GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0 owner
candidates.contract: One object-predicate consuming transition per token; fresh JDK node graphs own repetition, branches and captures. Snapshot inputs preserve nulls and identity. Visible failed-result validity is separate from engine search positions. Existing character Pattern/Matcher source remains unchanged.
candidates.complexity: O(pattern occurrences) graph per compilation and O(input tokens) snapshot. Existing JDK backtracking time and stack characteristics; possible exponential matching. No performance claim.
candidates.upstream_expression: Group quantifier orchestration adapted from GPL2+Classpath Pattern.group0 with Oracle notice retained. Existing engine algorithms are called directly.

behavioral_contracts.unit: One input list element, including null. No serialization, lexer or token identity encoding.
behavioral_contracts.predicate: Predicate<? super T> receives original token; stable within an operation and may be repeated. Original exceptions propagate; no matcher reentry.
behavioral_contracts.snapshot: Defensive shallow input copy; immutable list views retain token identity and nulls. Caller list and shared toArray output cannot mutate the snapshot.
behavioral_contracts.composition: Sequence order and ordered alternatives; fresh graph/group/local slots for every occurrence. Empty sequence is allowed; zero alternatives rejected.
behavioral_contracts.repetition: Inclusive nonnegative bounds; GREEDY, RELUCTANT, POSSESSIVE; Integer.MAX_VALUE means unbounded. Existing group algorithms own nullable and capture selection.
behavioral_contracts.captures: Left-to-right preorder numbering, enclosing before contents, unique ASCII letter/alphanumeric names. Empty participating groups and absent groups distinguished.
behavioral_contracts.coordinates: Absolute half-open token indices; absent start/end=-1 and list/span=null.
behavioral_contracts.state: Every completed false matching operation invalidates visible captures, including exhausted empty search. Invalid region/find(start) and failed snapshot reset preserve prior state. Reset after callback exceptions.
behavioral_contracts.search: Nonoverlapping results; zero-length result advances next start by one token. Explicit find(start) restores full input region.
behavioral_contracts.scope: No textual regex parser, lexer, backreference/lookaround builders, complete T-Rex grammar compatibility or new JNI callback path.
behavioral_contracts.threading: Independent mutable matchers; shared patterns require thread-safe predicates and literal values.

counterexample_refinements.finding: Existing Matcher early exhaustion may retain first while clearing group slots.
counterexample_refinements.selected_fix: Independent TokenMatcher.matched validity and requireMatch; engine positions unchanged.
counterexample_refinements.verification: Full accessor invalidation, null-name ordering, repeated exhaustion and range-failure preservation.

counterexample_refinements.witness: (a|ab){0,4}b on abb and nested nullable captures
counterexample_refinements.finding: Arbitrary branch repetition must retain internal alternative backtracking.
counterexample_refinements.selected_fix: Pattern.group0 GroupCurly versus Loop/LazyLoop decisions, Branch optional and Curly possessive.
counterexample_refinements.verification: Generated typed-vs-character AST differentials and independent language oracle.

counterexample_refinements.finding: Unescaped delimiter serialization conflates different token sequences.
counterexample_refinements.selected_fix: Direct predicate on original snapshot element at one token index.
counterexample_refinements.verification: Delimiter and supplementary payloads, toString throws and 65537 object identities.
